newsitem.title: HONG KONG: SHK Prop to launch HK$10.5 billion loan.
newsitem.headline: SHK Prop to launch HK$10.5 billion loan.

text.p: Sun Hung Kai Properties plans to raise funds via a HK$10.5 billion loan facility, the company said on Tuesday.
The issue will be launched into general syndication shortly, SHK Properties said.

The facility was 1.68 times oversubscribed in the underwriting phase to HK$13.4 billion from the HK$5 billion initially proposed, but allocations have been scaled back to HK$10.5 billion, the company said.
The deal has a final maturity of seven years and pays an interest margin of 48 basis points over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate.
The issue is a revolving credit in the first three years of its life and converts to a term loan thereafter.
Proceeds are to be used for refinancing some of the issuer's existing debts and for general working capital

Arrangers and senior underwriters are BNP, Chase Manhattan Asia, Hang Seng Bank, Societe Generale Asia, Standard Chartered Bank, Sumitomo Bank, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi, Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank, Fuji Bank, Industrial Bank of Japan, JP Morgan Securities Asia, Sakura Bank, Sanwa Bank, HypoBank and Bayerische Landesbank.
Arrangers and underwriters are ABN Amro Bank, Citibank, Dresdner Bank, UBS, Credit Lyonnais, CS First Boston, LTCB Japan, Mitsubishi Trust and Banking Corp, Tokai Bank and WestLB.
